subject: Phased reintegration and check-ins for parental return - Janet Suarez
messages:
From: Janet Suarez <janet.suarez@example.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Returning part-time from parental leave - request to discuss phased schedule

Hi Evelyn (and Marissa),

I hope you both are well. I wanted to share that my pediatrician and I feel ready for me to begin a gradual return to work starting the week of May 18th. My doctor has provided a note recommending a phased schedule (4 hours/day for the first 2 weeks, then 6 hours/day for the next 4 weeks) and flexibility for a morning pumping break and one mid-day break as needed. I'm attaching the medical note.

Before I confirm dates, I wanted to check in with you about coverage, priorities, and what a successful reintegration looks like from your perspective. I'm happy to start with a reduced scope (tactically owning two active tickets and pairing on on-call for one shift) to ease back in.

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync next week? I can be flexible on times.

Thanks,
Janet Suarez
Senior Software Engineer - Inference
janet.suarez@example.com
+1 (415) 555-1284

Subject: Re: Returning part-time from parental leave - request to discuss phased schedule

Thanks for the note and congrats, Janet — and thanks for flagging the doctor's recommendations. I appreciate you proposing a concrete phased schedule; that makes planning much easier.

Quick thoughts:
- I agree with starting May 18th with the 4-hr/day cadence for two weeks, then increasing to 6-hr/day for the following month, subject to check-ins.
- We'll temporarily reassign triage for the realtime-agg pipeline to Laura for the first two weeks to keep your context preserved but lower the interruption risk.
- Please plan to own the two active tickets you mentioned (INF-421, INF-434). I'll keep you off rotation for the on-call shift for the first two weeks, then we'll reassess.

Would 10:00am PT on Tuesday May 12th for a 30-min sync work for you? I want Marissa on the call to walk through formal paperwork and accommodations (partner time-off policy, FMLA check, and our RTW template).

I'll draft a short reintegration checklist and an interim schedule spreadsheet and share them after the call.

—Eve
Evelyn Hart
Engineering Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Thanks for looping me in. A few HR items to cover on our call on May 12th at 10:00am PT (invite sent):

1) Paperwork: I'll send the short RTW acknowledgement for signatures (DocuSign link included below). We'll also confirm FMLA/CFRA status and any state-specific leave paperwork.
2) Accommodations: We support reduced hours, pumped-breaks, and flexible start times. Please note: to maintain benefits continuity we'll confirm the effective dates for payroll adjustments; benefits remain active during the phased schedule.
3) Manager checklist: Evelyn, I'll need you to sign off on the interim schedule (who covers triage, who pairs on what, expected deliverables by the first 30/60/90 days).
4) Wellness check-ins: Standard cadence is weekly for the first month, then biweekly for the next two months — but we'll tailor to Janet's needs.

Attachments I'm sharing now: RTW_playbook_JSuarez_v1.pdf and a blank interim_schedule_may-july.xlsx (fill and return after the call).

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/RTW/0b3f-RTW-ack-janet

Best,

Subject: Finalized phased reintegration plan and next steps (starts May 18)

Janet — thanks again for the convo this morning. Summarizing the plan we agreed on and next steps so everything is in writing: 

Plan summary (effective May 18):
- May 18–29: 4 hours/day, flexible start between 8:30–10:30am, daily 30-min pumping break as needed. No on-call. Own INF-421 and INF-434 with Laura covering triage. Weekly 30-minute check-ins with me (Mon 9am PT).
- June 1–June 26: 6 hours/day, flexible start between 8:00–10:00am. Resume light on-call pairing twice in the month (no solo paging). Weekly check-ins drop to biweekly depending on energy.
- Documentation: Marissa sent the RTW_playbook and interim schedule. Please review and e-sign the DocuSign consent by EOD May 11.
- Ergonomics: Laura will coordinate a brief remote ergonomic check the first week back and order a lumbar pillow if requested.

Action items:
- Janet: e-sign DocuSign, fill interim schedule with preferred working blocks, and upload any additional medical notes to HR (done).
- Evelyn: finalize ticket reassignments and post a blurred status in #infra so the on-call buddy knows coverage.
- Marissa: finalize payroll adjustments and confirm benefits status for the phased period.

Attachments included: RTW_playbook_JSuarez_v1.pdf, interim_schedule_may-july.xlsx (filled), medical_note_emily_20260501.pdf

If anything needs to change after the first weekly check-in, we'll adjust. Welcome back in whichever cadence is best for you — we'll prioritize health and sustainable ramp.

—Eve
Evelyn Hart
